pick: pure-rand xoroshiro128plus(54017): one uniformInt per genre in order catch, whack, defense, slice, hop, crowd, merge, push, then 2 more from the remaining dev targets

pairs.text: a bear catches falling honey jars in a basket
pairs.why: Game A shows movement around a broad arena, glowing projectiles, and enemies that build up to a large foe close to the player near the end. Game B has a few falling objects above a small platform, with less variety and little visible escalation before it ends.

pairs.text: catch raindrops in a cup but not the lightning bolts
pairs.why: Game B keeps drops, coins, and black hazards close to the player on a small platform, creating more immediate action and danger before it ends. Game A shows scattered glowing objects across a large grassy field, with the player often out of view and little visible buildup.

pairs.text: place cannons to hold the lanes against invading crabs on the beach
pairs.why: Game B shows a cannon tracking several crabs across the beach, with crabs moving closer and visible shots and health bars adding action toward the end. Game A mostly repeats the same sparse lanes with an occasional distant crab and a turtle shifting along the bottom, showing less danger or buildup.

pairs.text: merge the same animals into bigger ones without filling the box
pairs.why: Game B keeps threats close to the orange player, with marked figures, particle bursts, and a growing crowd that builds to large orange obstacles across the walkway. Game A shows falling figures and accumulating yellow balls, but most activity stays far below the player on the top platform, making it feel less immediate and varied.

pairs.text: a bunny hops across train tracks and busy streets to get home
pairs.why: Game A repeatedly surrounds the player with dense moving traffic, with rivers, logs, and a railway adding variety and sustained danger through the final scenes. Game B has jumps across gaps and occasional spikes, but its spacious platforms and sparse hazards make the action look less intense and the ending less built up.

pairs.text: push the crabs off a shrinking island
pairs.why: Game B keeps the green player close to several red enemies in a small arena, with a thick red boundary and more clustered threats building tension later. Game A has a richer desert scene, but much of the play appears spread across empty ground with distant threats and only a late close encounter.

pairs.text: gather more soldiers at gates and fight the boss at the end of the bridge
pairs.why: Game A offers frequent gate choices, a visibly growing crowd, and a large enemy near the finish followed by a sharp loss of runners. Game B has scattered glowing objects and later enemies, including a large pursuer, but much of the play takes place in a mostly empty arena with threats farther apart.

pairs.text: slash the bouncing slimes before they fall back down
pairs.why: Game A shows close enemies, repeated bright attack effects, and a much larger enemy appearing later, giving the fight variety and escalation. Game B mostly shows the fox moving between five platforms in an otherwise empty field, with only occasional small objects and little visible buildup.

pairs.text: cut the flying donuts with a laser sword in space
pairs.why: Game A shows the player moving across platforms as rings, glowing balls, and flying objects appear nearby, with more airborne action toward the end. Game B spends most of its time pressed against a large blank wall that obscures the action, then briefly reveals rocky terrain before ending.

pairs.text: whack the moles popping out of the garden holes
pairs.why: Game B shows movement among scattered creatures and obstacles, with a large enemy close to the player and a shrinking health bar creating a late fight. Game A mostly repeats movement beside five holes and a mallet, with little visible escalation before it ends.
